content.title: Oscars winners, see the full list at the 98th Academy Awards
content.text: Madigan went on to win the first award of the night for best supporting actress for her work in “Weapons.” Acknowledging that many winners reel off a long list of names in their acceptance speeches, she said, “They’re people that mean something to you, that you couldn’t be there without them.” Though “Sinners” had come into the night with a record-setting number of nominations, “One Battle” ended up with the most wins, with six, and “Sinners” followed with four.Get Starting PointA guide through the most important stories of the morning, delivered Monday through Friday.Netflix’s “KPop Demon Hunters” took home the award for best animated feature, with co-director Maggie Kang saying, “This is for Korea, and for Koreans everywhere,” acknowledging that it had taken a long time for animated movies to feature people who look like her.“Tell your story, sing in your voice. I promise you the world is waiting,” said co-director Chris Applehans.The night also featured a nod to the upcoming “The Devil Wears Prada” sequel, with star Anne Hathaway coming out to present the costume and makeup/hairstyling awards alongside longtime Vogue editor Anna Wintour, who (allegedly) inspired the title character. “Frankenstein” won both awards, but “Prada” fans no doubt enjoyed Wintour viciously calling Hathaway “Emily.”This year, the ceremony debuted a new award, for best casting, and performers from each nominated film came out to present. The award went to Cassandra Kulukundis, who pulled together a cast including Leonardo DiCaprio, Sean Penn, Benicio del Toro, Teyana Taylor, Regina Hall, and newcomer Chase Infiniti in “One Battle After Another.”Kieran Culkin, a winner last year for best supporting actor, presented this year’s award, which was won by Sean Penn for his work on “One Battle After Another,” then quipped, “Sean Penn couldn’t be here this evening, or didn’t want to, so I’ll be accepting the award on his behalf.”“Sinners” won the Oscar for best original screenplay, while Paul Thomas Anderson won his first Oscar for his adapted screenplay for “One Battle After Another.” He went on to win for best director as well.With some high profile deaths this year, the “in memoriam” segment was structured slightly differently. It began with a moment dedicated to the late writer and director Rob Reiner and his wife Michelle, a photographer, from actor Billy Crystal, a star of “When Harry Met Sally,” who called their loss “immeasurable,” and closed with a heartfelt, “Buddy, what fun we had storming the castle.”Rachel McAdams came out to speak about the late Diane Keaton (the two were costars in “The Family Stone”). She tearfully recounted how much of an inspiration Keaton had been, and said she had a habit of reciting the classic song “Make new friends, but keep the old” on set. Singer Barbra Streisand also appeared to speak about her late “The Way We Were” costar, Robert Redford. “Bob had real backbone, on and off the screen,” she said, praising his protection of freedom of the press and his support of up and coming directors at the Sundance Film Festival. She then performed a couple of lines from “The Way We Were.”With her win for best cinematography for “Sinners,” Autumn Durald Arkapaw made history as the first woman (and first Black person) to win the award. She was only the second female nominee in the category’s history. In her speech, she shouted out the first woman to be nominated in that category, Rachel Morrison (“Mudbound”), and Spike Lee’s frequent cinematographer, Ellen Kuras.The best actor race seemed to have developed into something of a neck and neck battle between Timothée Chalamet and Michael B. Jordan; Jordan ended up winning for his dual role in “Sinners.” He thanked director Ryan Coogler for “betting on original ideas and original artistry.” And Jessie Buckley, long deemed the frontrunner for lead actress for her work in “Hamnet,” dedicated her eventual win to “the wonderful chaos of a mother’s heart.”“One Battle After Another” took home the prize for best picture. After honoring his cast, Anderson closed out the night with, “Let’s have a martini; this is pretty amazing.” See the full list of 2026 Oscar winners below.
